# Python fixture expectations

What each `python:` tooling entry in the audit skill family must observe when it runs against the seeded fixture partitions, written down before the run. Generated from `scripts/python_fixture_spec.py` by `scripts/render_python_fixture_expectations.py`: edit the module and re-render, never this file. The `--check` flag of that renderer is what holds the two together, and CI runs it.

The point of writing these down in advance is that a fixture whose expected output is not recorded first is just a smaller real target. Against a real repository an audit can only ask whether a command ran and returned something plausible; here the right answer is known before the tool speaks, so a tool that runs cleanly and reports half the truth fails instead of passing.

Every pin below was checked against OSV and PyPI on **2026-08-13**. That date is what the evidence column is worth: a pin is frozen, but the advisories against it only accumulate, so re-verifying one means querying both sources again and moving the date with it.

The fixture trees themselves are generated and never committed to this repository. Each one is a git repository of its own with every file committed inside it, because some tools read only tracked files. This record and the module it comes from are the committed half here.

## The shared dependency set

Every partition declares the same logical set in its own manifest format, so the set below is stated once rather than per partition. The expectation table further down is scoped where a partition changes the answer. 1 of the 5 entries are undeclared by design: they arrive transitively and are imported anyway, which is the seed a hygiene lens has to catch.

| Package | Pin | Imported | Seeds | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `jinja2` | `3.1.2` | yes | vulnerable, transitive-root | OSV: 10 advisories over CVE-2024-22195, CVE-2024-34064, CVE-2024-56201, CVE-2024-56326 and CVE-2025-27516; requires MarkupSafe, which is what makes it the transitive root. 2.11.3 carries four of the same CVEs and is not usable here: it imports soft_unicode, removed in markupsafe 2.1, so the seeded package would not import at all |
| `packaging` | `20.9` | yes | stale | no advisories; latest is 26.3, six majors ahead |
| `Unidecode` | `1.4.0` | yes | copyleft | classifier: GNU General Public License v2 or later (GPLv2+); pure Python, declares no dependencies of its own |
| `six` | `1.10.0` | no | declared-unused | no advisories; declared and never imported, which is deptry DEP002 |
| `markupsafe` | *(undeclared)* | yes | undeclared-import | arrives through jinja2 and is imported directly, which is deptry DEP003 |

## What each partition runs

`uv` carries every `python:` entry in the family, because it is the package manager the whole fixture set is built through: it resolves the tree, exports the requirements and PEP 751 partitions directly, and runs the poetry and pipenv lock steps as one-shot commands. The partition that has to answer every check is the one whose toolchain can build every fixture. The others carry the dependency records, which read each partition's own manifest and lock format and so ask a different question in each, plus `test/coverage-reach`, which exists to prove that partition's materialization route works rather than to re-test the tool.

| Partition | Expectations | Checks |
|---|---|---|
| `uv` | 26 | every check in the expectation table |
| `pip` | 7 | `deps/freshness`, `deps/hygiene`, `deps/inventory`, `deps/licenses`, `deps/transitive-licenses`, `deps/vulnerabilities`, `test/coverage-reach` |
| `poetry` | 7 | `deps/freshness`, `deps/hygiene`, `deps/inventory`, `deps/licenses`, `deps/transitive-licenses`, `deps/vulnerabilities`, `test/coverage-reach` |
| `pipenv` | 7 | `deps/freshness`, `deps/hygiene`, `deps/inventory`, `deps/licenses`, `deps/transitive-licenses`, `deps/vulnerabilities`, `test/coverage-reach` |
| `pylock` | 7 | `deps/freshness`, `deps/hygiene`, `deps/inventory`, `deps/licenses`, `deps/transitive-licenses`, `deps/vulnerabilities`, `test/coverage-reach` |

## Expected result per check

31 entries over 26 checks. A check whose answer differs by partition is written as one entry per scope, the scopes disjoint, rather than as one entry with a hedge - so a run against one partition has exactly one right answer to fail against.

The `Form` column takes one of `exact`, `floor`, `absence`. `exact` states an observation that is fully determined: a correct tool reports it, and output that differs is a finding about the tool whether it reports less or more. `floor` states a location and a minimum, for the entries where an exact number would go stale on its own - advisories accumulate against a frozen pin, a mutation count moves with the operator set, and a thinly exercised suite makes over-reporting the correct answer. `absence` states that there is nothing of this kind to find, so any hit is a false positive.

An entry with no seed is not an oversight: it states what a correct tool reports on a fixture that plants nothing for it, which is how a family finding is told apart from a fixture gap.

| Check | Partitions | Form | Seeds | Expected |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `deps/vulnerabilities` | all | floor | vulnerable | at least 5 distinct CVEs against jinja2 3.1.2: CVE-2024-22195, CVE-2024-34064, CVE-2024-56201, CVE-2024-56326, CVE-2025-27516. The floor is read out of the pin's own evidence rather than typed, so re-verifying the pin moves the floor with it instead of leaving the two to disagree. A floor rather than an exact count for two reasons: new advisories against a frozen pin only ever arrive, and tools report advisories rather than CVEs, several advisories mapping to one CVE - so a report of either satisfies this and the run records which unit it counted in |
| `deps/freshness` | all | exact | stale | every declared dependency except Unidecode is outdated, packaging 20.9 most obviously at six majors behind 26.3. Unidecode 1.4.0 is the latest release and is the control: a route that reports it outdated is producing a false positive, which an expectation naming all of them could never have caught. Named rather than counted, because the count moves with the dependency set while which one is the control does not |
| `deps/licenses` | all | exact | copyleft | Unidecode 1.4.0 is reported under a GPLv2+ licence. A copyleft entry the check must surface rather than a count |
| `deps/transitive-licenses` | all | floor | transitive-root | at least markupsafe appears as a transitive component with a licence, since it is never declared and arrives through jinja2 |
| `deps/hygiene` | `pipenv` | exact | - | deptry finds no dependency specification at all and raises DependencySpecificationNotFoundError. A Pipfile is not a format it reads, so this partition has no hygiene lens the harness can run on any grant: deptry is the only command the record offers for Python, and the manifest-and-lockfile read it also offers is a reading procedure rather than a command this round executes. That is a finding about the family rather than about the fixture, and is why this partition gets its own entry rather than being folded into the one the other partitions share |
| `deps/hygiene` | `uv`, `pip`, `poetry`, `pylock` | exact | declared-unused, undeclared-import | run as `deptry .` with its default excludes, six is reported declared-and-unused (DEP002) and markupsafe is reported as a transitive dependency being imported (DEP003). A further 2 DEP003 rows name fixture_app's own modules, one per file under src/ that imports the package by name, because deptry treats a src-layout package's self-imports as third-party. They are expected output rather than a seed, and the run records them as the tool's behaviour on this layout instead of configuring them away, since suppressing them would hide a false positive an audited project would also meet. The scan root is stated because the answer moves with it - `deptry src` makes the package local and those rows vanish - and the record prescribes no root, which is a gap in the record |
| `deps/inventory` | `uv` | exact | - | `uv export --format=cyclonedx1.5 --frozen` emits CycloneDX 1.5 listing the 4 declared dependencies plus markupsafe and pyparsing, both transitive. The record names this command for a uv-locked partition, cyclonedx-py having no uv subcommand, so the route is the record's rather than the audit's invention. The harness carries it as the prescribed command of its cyclonedx-py entry for this partition, and puts nothing in front of it: the command names its own runner, so fronting it with the fetch that entry's tool name resolves to would obtain a package it never calls. No component carries a licences field, which is a family finding rather than a fixture gap: no route this record offers populates licences on any partition, so an SBOM is not where this family's licence evidence comes from and deps/licenses owns it alone |
| `deps/inventory` | `pip` | exact | - | `cyclonedx-py requirements` emits exactly the 4 declared dependencies and nothing else: a requirements.txt carries no transitive resolution, so markupsafe is absent, and no component carries a licences field. Both absences are correct tool behaviour on this input rather than misses, which is why this partition is written as its own entry - an SBOM expectation naming markupsafe would grade a working tool against a claim its input cannot support |
| `deps/inventory` | `pipenv` | exact | - | `cyclonedx-py pipenv` reads Pipfile.lock and emits CycloneDX 1.6 listing the 4 declared dependencies plus markupsafe and pyparsing. No licences field, as on every other route here |
| `deps/inventory` | `poetry` | exact | - | cyclonedx-py's poetry subcommand fails with CRITICAL \| CDX > 'name' and writes no SBOM, because it reads name from [tool.poetry] and this partition carries PEP 621 metadata, which is the form poetry 2 pushes projects towards and the form that emits no deprecation warning. Measured both ways on one tree with one tool: the legacy all-in-[tool.poetry] manifest produces a valid CycloneDX 1.6 document, so the finding is that the subcommand has no route for PEP 621 poetry metadata rather than no poetry route at all. Recorded before the run precisely so PR 2 cannot mistake the narrow claim for the broad one |
| `deps/inventory` | `pylock` | exact | - | none of this record's prescribed SBOM routes reads PEP 751. `uv export --frozen` refuses, because this partition carries no uv.lock by construction; cyclonedx-py has no pylock subcommand; and its requirements subcommand pointed at pylock.toml does not refuse either - it reads the TOML as requirement lines and emits a document that fails its own 1.6 schema validation, exiting non-zero having written nothing usable. A family finding, and the sharpest one this partition exists to produce: the record's Python fallback names no route for the lock format PEP 751 standardises, and the nearest tool produces garbage rather than an error a caller could distinguish from a tool that found nothing. Scoped to this record's own routes on purpose - the format is readable, `uv pip install -r pylock.toml` resolves the partition and is how it is materialized, so the gap is in the inventory tooling rather than in the ecosystem's support for the format |
| `test/coverage-reach` | all | exact | uncovered-branch | the two guard branches of fixture_app.invariant.clamp are among the uncovered set rather than the whole of it: the seeded suite imports only render and invariant, so every module no test imports reports at zero as well. Written as membership because a report listing all of them is correct output, and an expectation naming only clamp would read that correctness as over-reporting. On a thin partition this doubles as proof the materialization route works, since pytest-cov is tiered target-execution and answers nothing unless the tree resolved and the suite ran |
| `arch/complexity` | `uv` | exact | complexity | fixture_app.complexity.classify is over the default threshold of every tool the record names: ruff C901 computes 12 against its default of 10, radon rates it C at 13, and xenon fails --max-absolute B on it. The two engines differ by one because ruff does not walk conditional expressions, so the seed is written with explicit branches throughout and both clear their thresholds with margin rather than one landing exactly on its default, where C901's `>` would let it pass in silence |
| `arch/complexity-gate` | `uv` | absence | - | no complexity threshold is configured anywhere in the fixture, so the expected finding is the absence of a gate rather than a hit. This is why arch/complexity is seeded above every tool's default rather than fixed by configuring one: a threshold added to make that check fire would falsify this one |
| `arch/cycles` | `uv` | exact | cycle | one cycle, between fixture_app.domain.model and fixture_app.infra.store |
| `arch/layering` | `uv` | exact | layering | fixture_app.domain.model imports fixture_app.infra.store, which is the layering violation |
| `arch/coupling` | `uv` | floor | cycle | the two modules in the cycle are each other's dependents, so neither is a leaf |
| `arch/over-decomposition` | `uv` | exact | pass-through | the record's Python fallback triggers on modules whose functions only forward to another module, and the fixture has exactly two: fixture_app.domain.model.load forwards to fixture_app.infra.store.read, and fixture_app.infra.store.load_via_domain forwards to fixture_app.domain.model.load. The package is 10 files under src/, which supplies the long tail of one-symbol modules the same fallback names. Both are Minor on the record's own band, and neither becomes a finding without the read the record requires before a count counts - so the expected observation is the pair, not a verdict on them |
| `arch/over-abstraction` | `uv` | exact | single-caller | three triggers from the record's Python fallback, which says one call site is the trigger for a single-function module: fixture_app.deadcode.never_referenced has zero call sites and fixture_app.invariant.clamp has one. The third is clamp's low and high parameters, each bound to a single distinct value across that one call site, which the same fallback calls an unexercised knob. All Minor, and as with over-decomposition the record requires a read before a count becomes a finding |
| `arch/martin-metrics` | `uv` | exact | - | neither module in the cycle lands in a zone. The record defines I = Ce/(Ca+Ce), and a mutual cycle forces Ca = Ce = 1 on both sides, so I = 0.5 for each; the fixture declares no ABC, Protocol or @abstractmethod anywhere, so A = 0 and D = \|A + I - 1\| = 0.5. That is the main sequence, not the zone of pain (A and I both near 0) or of uselessness (both near 1). A cycle is the mechanism that pulls modules towards the main sequence, so no cycle can ever seed this metric's subject. Nothing here is planted for it: a fixture gap rather than a family finding, since the tool is not being asked something it fails to answer |
| `arch/hidden-coupling` | `uv` | absence | - | nothing is seeded outside the import graph. Both edges of the cycle are plain top-level import statements, which is exactly why arch/cycles sees them, and the fixture's only module-level mutable state is read within its own module. The record's subject is coupling that does not travel through an import, so a report here is a false positive and the check's real subject is a fixture gap |
| `arch/dead-code` | `uv` | floor | dead-code | fixture_app.deadcode.never_referenced appears among the unused symbols. A floor rather than an exact claim because several other seeded functions are also never called - the seeded suite exercises the package thinly on purpose - so a tool naming only this one and a tool naming every function both satisfy the check, and the run records which it was |
| `security/dangerous-calls` | `uv` | exact | dangerous-calls | the eval call in fixture_app.unsafe.run_expression |
| `security/injection` | `uv` | exact | injection | the shell=True subprocess in fixture_app.unsafe.run_shell and the string-formatted SQL in fixture_app.unsafe.query |
| `security/crypto` | `uv` | exact | crypto | the md5 digest in fixture_app.unsafe.digest |
| `security/unsafe-io` | `uv` | exact | unsafe-io | the unchecked tarfile.extractall in fixture_app.unsafe.unpack and the bare xml.etree parse in fixture_app.unsafe.parse_document. These are seeded for this check specifically: its record scopes itself to XXE, archive extraction and symlink following, none of which eval, shell=True, built SQL or md5 are, so without them bandit's shell rule would fire and make the check look exercised while its own subject went untested |
| `docs/docstring-coverage` | `uv` | exact | undocumented | fixture_app.unsafe is the one non-empty module under src/ with no module docstring, so it carries the seed. It is not alone: 7 of the seeded files have no module docstring, the others being the empty package __init__ files and those seeded test files that open with code, so a per-file report names them too and the expectation is that unsafe.py is among them rather than the only one. Written that way because naming one file would make correct output read as over-reporting. Function-level coverage is low across the whole seeded package rather than in that file alone, so the percentage each tool reports is recorded at the run rather than predicted here |
| `test/determinism` | `uv` | exact | order-dependence | tests/test_order.py fails under a randomized order and passes in file order. The shuffle seed that reproduces the failure is measured when the fixture is first built and recorded in the build smoke record, never guessed: it is a property of pytest-randomly's ordering rather than of this definition, so stating a value here would be the guess the round exists to remove |
| `test/isolation` | `uv` | exact | slow-test | tests/test_slow.py::test_slow_but_passing sleeps 2s and so exceeds a pytest-timeout of 1s, while passing with no timeout configured. Both numbers are interpolated from the module constants the seeded file itself is written from, because the sleep and the timeout are one fact and lowering either alone would retire the seed in silence |
| `test/mutation` | `uv` | floor | mutation-survivor | at least one surviving mutant in fixture_app.invariant.clamp, whose two guard branches no test asserts. A floor because the count moves with the operator set |
| `test/property-based-gap` | `uv` | exact | property-gap | fixture_app.invariant.clamp has an obvious invariant, low <= result <= high, and no property test anywhere in the fixture |

## Without the grant

Every entry above is run under two grant states, and the table above is the answer with the grant. Where withholding it changes the answer rather than removing it, the second answer is written out below - 8 of the 31 entries. The rest are derived from their check records and so are not restated per entry. On a record declaring `tooling:`, a check whose every Python tool carries a `needs` tier and whose `ungranted_note` is the `none` sentinel answers `no-evidence (not-permitted)` without the grant, and a check with an untiered Python tool answers its `claim` in both states. On a record declaring `routes:` the same two cases are read off the routes rather than off a note - a Python language whose every answering-kind, non-forbidden route needs the grant answers `no-evidence (not-permitted)`, and an untiered route left in that language is what still runs - and neither writes a second answer out here, because the routes counterpart of `ungranted_note` carries the sentinel and no prose of its own.

This axis exists because a correct ungranted run graded against the granted answer reads as a tool defect. The `deps/hygiene` rows below are the sharpest case, and they state the two answers rather than having them restated here, where the copy would be free to drift.

| Check | Partitions | Without the grant |
|---|---|---|
| `deps/freshness` | all | the same claim. The pins are in the clone, so the registry route the record prescribes answers this without the tree: the project endpoint reports the latest release, which is the comparison the tiered tools would have made. A partition reporting no-evidence here has skipped a route the record says survives a withheld grant, and that is the failure to look for |
| `deps/licenses` | all | the same claim, from the registry rather than from an installed METADATA. Unidecode declares its licence as a classifier rather than as an SPDX expression, so this doubles as the control for the record's instruction to read all three metadata channels: a route reading only license_expression reports the one copyleft dependency in the set as unlicensed, which is a false clean rather than a miss |
| `deps/transitive-licenses` | all | the same route as deps/licenses, applied to the whole locked graph rather than the declared set, and conditional on the partition's lockfile pinning that graph. Where it pins only the direct dependencies there is nothing to enumerate markupsafe from, and the record names that as not a clean result for the partition rather than as a pass. The run records which partitions fell which way; a partition reported clean here without a transitive pin set is the false clean this axis exists to catch |
| `deps/hygiene` | `pipenv` | the same, and for the same reason: the format is unreadable to deptry with the tree or without it, so this is the one entry here the grant cannot move |
| `deps/hygiene` | `uv`, `pip`, `poetry`, `pylock` | six is still DEP002, but markupsafe is reported DEP001 (missing) rather than DEP003, because nothing without the tree tells deptry that markupsafe ships under jinja2. That is the record's own note - the scanner misreports in both directions at once - and it is the reason this axis is written down at all: graded against the granted claim, a correct ungranted run reads as a tool defect |
| `test/coverage-reach` | all | the reach measurement does not survive the withheld grant, but the check is not no-evidence: what is excluded from measurement is readable in the clone, and this fixture configures no [tool.coverage.run] source or omit and no [tool.coverage.report] exclude_lines. So the expected ungranted answer is that nothing is excluded, with the reach half unmeasured - and a run recording no-evidence for the whole check has skipped the half the record says survives |
| `test/determinism` | `uv` | the grep axis answers without the tree, and finds nothing: the seeded suite calls no time.time(), no datetime.now(), no unseeded random. and no network. Order-dependence itself goes unmeasured, which the record names as exactly the half a withheld grant costs - so the expected ungranted answer is a clean grep axis and an unmeasured order axis, not no-evidence for the check |
| `test/isolation` | `uv` | the I/O axis answers without the tree and finds nothing: the seeded suite makes no network, filesystem or database call, and raises no timeout in configuration. The duration evidence is what the grant buys, so the record prescribes answering on the I/O axis rather than reporting the check no-evidence as a whole |

## A seed nothing expects

A seeded finding that no expectation names would be planted and then never looked for, which at review is indistinguishable from a fixture that never planted it. So the two sets are held equal in both directions by the suite rather than by reading.

None: all 17 seeds the source files plant are named by some expectation. The dependency set plants its own, counted separately.

A seed that is expected and that no *tool* reports is a different thing and is not knowable from here - it is a finding about the skill family rather than a bug in the fixture, it is recorded as such when the fixtures are run, and the seed stays, because removing it would erase the evidence that the family has a hole there.
